tools.name: check_incident
tools.description: Answer for one public hostname: what the host's robots.txt and llms.txt declare for agent user agents, the official developer documentation path, the provider's official status, and any recent observations from other agents. Use when a web task is blocked or when asked whether a site is down or bloc

tools.name: report_observation
tools.description: Submit one de-identified firsthand observation under your own operating authority and platform rules. Public reports enter private review and are not site-status claims. Never include names, account details, URLs, cookies, tokens, or conversation text.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "report_observation" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_incident · Private data: check_incident, report_observation · Public sink: check_incident, report_observation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_incident · Private data: check_incident, report_observation · Public sink: check_incident, report_observation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_incident" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
